title: FENB / A day of changes
description: Standalone DX9 demonstrations of the features added or refined on 18 November 2026. Procedural scenery, read-only local Flyff textures and FENB's actual effect implementations. These are rendered demonstrations, not screenshots from a running game.

cards.title: Dense 3D grass
cards.description: Optional instanced blades planted on the existing terrain. The camera, ground texture and lighting are identical. Wind is frozen for this still.

cards.title: Snowy vegetation
cards.description: The independent snowy-grass option adds varied winter plants to recognized snow terrain. Ground and tree materials stay unchanged in this comparison.

cards.title: Fine, matte ground snow
cards.description: The current snow material preserves the painted texture while adding cool, fine-grained shading. A low camera makes the surface easier to inspect; this is a material effect, not extra snow geometry.

cards.title: Matching winter-tree snow
cards.description: The material treatment matches recognized snow on winter bark and foliage to the ground. The replacement-tree switch is off on both sides.

cards.title: Experimental tree bark
cards.description: FENB replaces an exactly recognized Flaris bark texture with its embedded artwork. Geometry and foliage are identical; Materials is off in both frames.

cards.title: Experimental Azria bark
cards.description: The same independent tree replacement on an exactly recognized Azria bark texture. The snowy crown is unchanged in this pair.

cards.title: Rain puddles / paving
cards.description: Rain gradually fills irregular world-anchored pools. Compare the sky and visible-tree reflections. The actual accumulation code advances through 20 seconds of full rain; fill time is shortened for the demo. SSR can only reflect visible scene information.

cards.title: Rain puddles / grassy ground
cards.description: The grass-material coverage control produces smaller, fragmented pools. Generated grass is off so that the wet ground can be inspected clearly.

cards.title: Rain puddles / soil
cards.description: The same camera over soil shows its independent puddle coverage. Paving, grass and soil use distinct receiver identities; unknown surfaces and snow are excluded.

cards.title: Refinement / drifting mist
cards.description: Identical paired source quads and alpha history: original refinement sprites become connected, dissipating mist. The test fixture supplies three isolated model scopes, as the supported native renderer does.

cards.title: Custom refinement colors
cards.description: The actual refinement color override applied to identical source geometry. These renders show the resulting color; the panel provides a hue wheel plus RGB and HEX inputs.

cards.title: Hide other players
cards.description: Blue figures represent other players. Their draws are filtered by FENB's shipping visibility predicate. Monsters, pets, the local player at left and the peaceful NPC at right remain. Synthetic actors demonstrate the filter, not game character models.

cards.title: Hide monsters
cards.description: The horned orange figures are filtered independently. Other players and pets remain. The actual rendering predicate is used; this offline scene does not simulate combat or networking.

cards.title: Hide pets
cards.description: The small gold figures are filtered independently. Other players, monsters, the local player and the peaceful NPC retain their draws.

cards.title: Independent draw distances
cards.description: Other players, monsters and pets have separate camera-distance limits. The demo uses 18 / 23 / 28 units respectively. Each individual example below uses an 18-unit limit for one category only. The local player and peaceful NPC remain.

cards.title: SSAO / fading native grass
cards.description: A regression comparison: both sides have SSAO enabled. Previously, translucent native grass cards could write opaque rectangles into depth. The current per-draw guard preserves their native color and blending while keeping those rectangles out of SSAO.
